clue.text: Quick animal to run after money bet

indicators.note: after places the word for running behind the word for the stake

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up before a hand of poker
to lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: A punter dashes off to chase down money he has wagered.
explanation.definitionFit: This hoofed African grazer is famous for its speed, so a quick animal describes it well.

clue.text: All points covered in a royal reply

indicators.note: covered in means the compass letters sit wrapped inside the outer pair

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Rex or Regina, the royal title
the four compass points are North, South, West and East

explanation.surface: Every point is addressed in a reply from royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts NSWE inside A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is a response given back, a close synonym.

clue.text: Using pill, fit to enter race

indicators.note: to enter tells us the word for fit goes inside the race letters

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
fit means able, capable of doing something

explanation.surface: An athlete on medication is declared fit to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is only a link word; TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle race, is a staple crossword race.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a small compressed dose of medicine, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Not much left-let it out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the phrase let it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says there is not much left and tells you to let it go.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hyphen hides that 'let it' is anagram material, rearranged by 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount, the sense in 'a little', means not much.

clue.text: Wine society opening in naval city

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A wine club holds its launch party in a naval town.
explanation.definitionFit: This English city on the south coast is the home of the Royal Navy, hence naval city.

clue.text: Obsession to replace receiver

definitions.meaning: a fixation or psychological complex someone cannot shake off
to put the telephone handset back and end the call

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a fixation, and the verb phrase means ending a phone call by putting down the handset.

clue.text: It's farewell to France

parts.note: reads as saying goodbye to the country, but means the phrase a French speaker uses for goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone is bidding goodbye to France.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase is the everyday way of saying goodbye, until we see each other again.

clue.text: Greed is nothing new for some Northerners

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Greed is a novelty among certain people from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: Geordies are natives of Tyneside in north-east England, so some Northerners in British terms.

clue.text: Do a strip poorly burlesque performer

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly executed striptease by a burlesque artiste.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mocks by comic imitation; burlesque is that kind of mocking performance.

clue.text: Call for help about British politician, a sad tale

indicators.note: about means the distress call goes around the British abbreviation

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's emergency plea becomes a tale of woe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the distress call around the British abbreviation, splitting it before the politician joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearful account told to win pity is a sad tale, the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: One's strong suit

parts.note: reads like a person's speciality, but means a suit literally made strong, of metal, worn by a knight

explanation.surface: Someone's area of particular expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate mail is a protective metal suit, so a strong suit in the literal sense.

clue.text: Look at good girl through monocle

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
lass is a northern word for a girl

explanation.surface: Ogling a nice girl through a single lens.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens worn in one eye, a kind of corrective glass.

clue.text: David ran back with Edward and escaped

indicators.note: ran back tells us to read the name backwards

parts.note: Dave is a short form of David
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named David and Edward ran off together and got away.
explanation.definitionFit: To have avoided capture or got away is a synonym for escaped.

clue.text: In which one had motion carried by two

definitions.text: In which one had motion carried by two

parts.words: In which one had motion carried by two
parts.note: sounds like a proposal backed by two voters, but describes a covered seat on poles borne by a pair of porters

explanation.surface: A meeting where a motion was passed by two votes.
explanation.definitionFit: This enclosed seat for one passenger was carried on poles by two bearers in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Beauty appears, holding marriage certificate

indicators.note: holding means the word for appears wraps around the certificate

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive
marriage lines is an old British phrase for a marriage certificate

explanation.surface: A bride looks lovely as she shows off her marriage certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marriage lines' is a dated British term for a marriage certificate; 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: This rather old-fashioned noun means pleasing looks, hence a synonym of beauty.

clue.text: Money lent to get home

parts.note: sounds like a loan for the fare back, but means a loan secured to buy a house

explanation.surface: Someone borrows cash for the journey back home.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a loan from a bank or building society used to buy property.

clue.text: In stress, I'd have mishap

indicators.note: In means the I'd letters go inside the word for stress

parts.note: accent means emphasis or stress on a syllable
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Under pressure, someone suffers a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is a link word; 'In stress' reads as 'under pressure' but 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky event, a close synonym.

clue.text: Surprised expression concealed by more confident witness

indicators.note: concealed by means the exclamation is tucked inside the word for more confident

parts.note: bolder means more daring or more confident
eh is an exclamation of surprise or query

explanation.surface: A gasp of surprise is suppressed by a more assured witness in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' signals the container; the exclamation sits after the first letter of the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sees something is a witness, as in beauty being in the eye of the onlooker.

clue.text: Clare Short's sort of music?

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters of the name are put in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of music the British politician Clare Short likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges CLARESHORT. Clare Short is a former UK Labour cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes music written for a full symphony band, so it relates to music.

clue.text: Put down contribution expected

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular contribution
due means expected, as a train due at noon

explanation.surface: A membership payment has been recorded and is anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a revolt is to quell or crush it, a synonym.

clue.text: Push the boat out-one in particular

definitions.meaning: to set a vessel afloat or start a venture
one particular kind of boat, a motor boat used for short trips

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to set a vessel going, and the noun is a specific type of small powered boat.

clue.text: Evasively answers the receivers

definitions.meaning: to fence with questions is to parry them, avoiding a direct reply
people who receive and sell on stolen goods

explanation.walkthrough: The grid as held reads PENCES, an OCR slip for FENCES.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means parries questions evasively, and the plural noun means dealers in stolen property.

clue.text: Slips up, retaining nothing in exam

indicators.note: retaining means the word for slips up holds the zero inside

parts.note: trips means stumbles or slips up
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A student makes errors and scores zero in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts O inside TRIPS. The answer is the Cambridge University honours exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The final honours examination at Cambridge University bears this name, so it is an exam.

clue.text: A leading Catholic clergyman is right

indicators.note: leading means take the first letter of Catholic

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A prominent Catholic priest is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading Catholic' gives C, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being correct, free from error, is what right means here.

clue.text: Discussion programme

parts.note: sounds like a TV debate show, but means the list of items for a meeting

explanation.surface: A TV or radio talk show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the list of topics to be discussed at a meeting, its programme of discussion.

clue.text: Complete heritage organisation in Ireland

indicators.note: in means the heritage letters are placed within the word for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the British body caring for historic buildings

explanation.surface: A whole conservation charity operating in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole, with nothing missing, is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Makes hole, say, in trousers

indicators.note: say tells us the word for makes hole is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: breaches means breaks through or makes a hole in

explanation.surface: Someone tears a hole in a pair of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are old-style trousers reaching just below the knee.
